e-5887.knowledge_point: Finding a Quadratic Polynomial Given Two Real Roots and a Leading Coefficient
e-5887.problem: The quadratic polynomial $P(x)$ has roots $x_1=2, x_2=5,$ and the coefficient of the quadratic term is $3.$ Find $P(x).$
e-5887.worked_solution:
Since our quadratic polynomial has roots ${\color{black}x_1=2}$ and ${\color{black}x_2=5},$ and the coefficient of the quadratic term is ${\color{black}a=3},$ we can write the polynomial as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}a(x-{x}_{1})(x-{x}_{2}) & =3(x-2)(x-5) \\  & =3(x-2)(x-5)\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the parentheses, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}3(x-2)(x-5) & =3({x}^{2}-7x+10) \\  & =3{x}^{2}-21x+30.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $P(x) = 3x^2-21x+30.$

e-5788.knowledge_point: Finding a Quadratic Polynomial Given a Double Root and a Leading Coefficient
e-5788.problem: The quadratic polynomial $P(x)$ has the double root $x_1=x_2=5,$ and the coefficient of the quadratic term is $a=1.$ Find $P(x).$
e-5788.worked_solution:
Since our quadratic polynomial has the double root ${\color{black}x_1=x_2=5},$ and the coefficient of the quadratic term is ${\color{black}a=1},$ we can write the polynomial as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}a(x-{x}_{1})^{2} & =1\cdot {(x-5)}^{2} \\  & ={(x-5)}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the parentheses, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{(x-5)}^{2} & ={x}^{2}-10x+25.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $P(x) = x^2 - 10x+25.$

e-5789.knowledge_point: Finding a Quadratic Polynomial Given Two Imaginary or Complex Roots
e-5789.problem: The quadratic polynomial $f(z)$ with real coefficients has roots $z_1=3+\textrm{i}$ and $z_2=3-\textrm{i},$ and the coefficient of the quadratic term is $2.$ Find $f(z).$
e-5789.worked_solution:
Since our quadratic polynomial has roots ${\color{black}z_1=3+\textrm{i}}$ and ${\color{black}z_2=3-\textrm{i}},$ and the coefficient of the quadratic term is ${\color{black}a=2},$ we can write the polynomial as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}a(z-{z}_{1})(z-{z}_{2}) & =2(z-(3+\text{i}))(z-(3-\text{i}))\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the parentheses, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}2(z-(3+\text{i}))(z-(3-\text{i})) & =2({z}^{2}-(3+\text{i})z-(3-\text{i})z+(3+\text{i})(3-\text{i})) \\  & =2({z}^{2}-(3+\text{i}+3-\text{i})z+({3}^{2}-{\text{i}}^{2})) \\  & =2({z}^{2}-6z+(9+1)) \\  & =2({z}^{2}-6z+10) \\  & =2{z}^{2}-12z+20.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $f(z) = 2z^2-12z+20.$

e-5791.knowledge_point: Factoring a Quadratic Polynomial With Complex Roots
e-5791.worked_solution:
First, we let $f(u) = u^2-2u+10.$

Next, we solve $f(u) = 0$ by completing the square, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(u) & =0 \\ {u}^{2}-2u+10 & =0 \\ ({u}^{2}-2u+{1}^{2})-{1}^{2}+10 & =0 \\ (u-1)^{2}-1+10 & =0 \\ (u-1)^{2}+9 & =0 \\ (u-1)^{2} & =-9 \\ (u-1)^{2} & =9{\text{i}}^{2} \\ (u-1)^{2} & =(3\text{i})^{2} \\ u-1 & =\pm 3\text{i} \\ u & =1\pm 3\text{i}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since our quadratic equation has roots $u_1=1+ 3\textrm{i}$ and $u_2=1- 3\textrm{i},$ and the coefficient of the quadratic term is $a=1,$ the expression $u^2-2u+10$ can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}{u}^{2}-2u+10 & =a(u-{u}_{1})(u-{u}_{2}) \\  & =(u-(1+3\text{i}))(u-(1-3\text{i})).\end{aligned}
$$

Question 3
?

The quadratic polynomial P(t) has roots t1=−5,t2=5, and the coefficient of the quadratic term is 4. Find P(t).

a
4t2+100
b
4t2−25
c
t2−25
d
4t2−100
e
t2+25
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

Since our quadratic polynomial has roots t1=−5 and t2=5, and the coefficient of the quadratic term is a=4, we can write the polynomial as follows:

a(t−t1)(t−t2)=(4)(t−(−5))(t−5)=4(t+5)(t−5)

Expanding the parentheses, we obtain

4(t+5)(t−5)=4(t2−25)=4t2−100.

Therefore, P(t)=4t2−100.

verification.explanation: The worked solution confirms P(t)=4(t+5)(t-5)=4(t^2-25)=4t^2-100, so option d is correct.

content.knowledge_point: Finding a Quadratic Polynomial Given Two Real Roots and a Leading Coefficient
content.problem: The quadratic polynomial $P(t)$ has roots ${t}_{1}=-5,{t}_{2}=5,$ and the coefficient of the quadratic term is $4.$ Find $P(t).$
content.worked_solution:
Since our quadratic polynomial has roots ${t}_{1}=-5$ and ${t}_{2}=5,$ and the coefficient of the quadratic term is $a=4,$ we can write the polynomial as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}a(t-{t}_{1})(t-{t}_{2}) & =(4)(t-(-5))(t-5) \\  & =4(t+5)(t-5)\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the parentheses, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}4(t+5)(t-5) & =4({t}^{2}-25) \\  & =4{t}^{2}-100.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $P(t)=4{t}^{2}-100.$

The quadratic polynomial P(t) has roots t1=4,t2=2, and the coefficient of the quadratic term is −3. Find P(t).

a
−3t2+18t+24
b
−3t2+6t−8
c
−3t2+18t−24
d
−3t2−24t−24
e
−3t2−6t+8

decision.explanation: With roots 4 and 2 and leading coefficient -3, P(t)=-3(t-4)(t-2)=-3(t^2-6t+8)=-3t^2+18t-24, which is option c.

after.name: Question 4
after.problem: The quadratic polynomial $P(t)$ has roots ${t}_{1}=4,{t}_{2}=2,$ and the coefficient of the quadratic term is $-3.$ Find $P(t).$
after.worked_solution:
Since our quadratic polynomial has roots ${t}_{1}=4$ and ${t}_{2}=2,$ and the coefficient of the quadratic term is $a=-3,$ we can write the polynomial as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}a(t-{t}_{1})(t-{t}_{2}) & =(-3)(t-4)(t-2) \\  & =(-3)(t-4)(t-2)\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the parentheses, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}(-3)(t-4)(t-2) & =(-3)({t}^{2}-6t+8) \\  & =-3{t}^{2}+18t-24.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $P(t)=-3{t}^{2}+18t-24.$

Question 4
?

The quadratic polynomial P(t) has roots t1=4,t2=2, and the coefficient of the quadratic term is −3. Find P(t).

a
−3t2+18t+24
b
−3t2+6t−8
c
−3t2+18t−24
d
−3t2−24t−24
e
−3t2−6t+8
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Since our quadratic polynomial has roots t1=4 and t2=2, and the coefficient of the quadratic term is a=−3, we can write the polynomial as follows:

a(t−t1)(t−t2)=(−3)(t−4)(t−2)=(−3)(t−4)(t−2)

Expanding the parentheses, we obtain

(−3)(t−4)(t−2)=(−3)(t2−6t+8)=−3t2+18t−24.

Therefore, P(t)=−3t2+18t−24.

content.knowledge_point: Finding a Quadratic Polynomial Given Two Real Roots and a Leading Coefficient
content.problem: The quadratic polynomial $P(t)$ has roots ${t}_{1}=4,{t}_{2}=2,$ and the coefficient of the quadratic term is $-3.$ Find $P(t).$
content.worked_solution:
Since our quadratic polynomial has roots ${t}_{1}=4$ and ${t}_{2}=2,$ and the coefficient of the quadratic term is $a=-3,$ we can write the polynomial as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}a(t-{t}_{1})(t-{t}_{2}) & =(-3)(t-4)(t-2) \\  & =(-3)(t-4)(t-2)\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the parentheses, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}(-3)(t-4)(t-2) & =(-3)({t}^{2}-6t+8) \\  & =-3{t}^{2}+18t-24.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $P(t)=-3{t}^{2}+18t-24.$

after.name: Question 5
after.problem: The quadratic polynomial $P(t)$ has roots ${t}_{1}=4,{t}_{2}=3,$ and the coefficient of the quadratic term is $2.$ Find $P(t).$
after.worked_solution:
Since our quadratic polynomial has roots ${t}_{1}=4$ and ${t}_{2}=3,$ and the coefficient of the quadratic term is $a=2,$ we can write the polynomial as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}a(t-{t}_{1})(t-{t}_{2}) & =(2)(t-4)(t-3) \\  & =2(t-4)(t-3)\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the parentheses, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}2(t-4)(t-3) & =2({t}^{2}-7t+12) \\  & =2{t}^{2}-14t+24.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $P(t)=2{t}^{2}-14t+24.$

Question 5
?

The quadratic polynomial P(t) has roots t1=4,t2=3, and the coefficient of the quadratic term is 2. Find P(t).

a
t2+7t−12
b
2t2−14t+24
c
2t2+24t−14
d
2t2−7t+12
e
t2+14t+24
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Since our quadratic polynomial has roots t1=4 and t2=3, and the coefficient of the quadratic term is a=2, we can write the polynomial as follows:

a(t−t1)(t−t2)=(2)(t−4)(t−3)=2(t−4)(t−3)

Expanding the parentheses, we obtain

2(t−4)(t−3)=2(t2−7t+12)=2t2−14t+24.

Therefore, P(t)=2t2−14t+24.

content.knowledge_point: Finding a Quadratic Polynomial Given Two Real Roots and a Leading Coefficient
content.problem: The quadratic polynomial $P(t)$ has roots ${t}_{1}=4,{t}_{2}=3,$ and the coefficient of the quadratic term is $2.$ Find $P(t).$
content.worked_solution:
Since our quadratic polynomial has roots ${t}_{1}=4$ and ${t}_{2}=3,$ and the coefficient of the quadratic term is $a=2,$ we can write the polynomial as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}a(t-{t}_{1})(t-{t}_{2}) & =(2)(t-4)(t-3) \\  & =2(t-4)(t-3)\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the parentheses, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}2(t-4)(t-3) & =2({t}^{2}-7t+12) \\  & =2{t}^{2}-14t+24.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $P(t)=2{t}^{2}-14t+24.$

The quadratic polynomial P(y) has the double root y1=y2=4, and the coefficient of the quadratic term is a=3. Find P(y).

a
3y2−4y+24
b
3y2−12y+32
c
3y2−8y+16
d
3y2−24y+48
e
3y2−3y+96

decision.explanation: A double root at 4 gives P(y)=3(y-4)^2=3(y^2-8y+16)=3y^2-24y+48, which is option d.

after.name: Question 6
after.problem: The quadratic polynomial $P(y)$ has the double root ${y}_{1}={y}_{2}=4,$ and the coefficient of the quadratic term is $a=3.$ Find $P(y).$
after.worked_solution:
Since our quadratic polynomial has the double root ${y}_{1}={y}_{2}=4,$ and the coefficient of the quadratic term is $a=3,$ we can write the polynomial as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}a(y-{y}_{1})^{2} & =3{(y-4)}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the parentheses, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}3{(y-4)}^{2} & =3({y}^{2}-8y+16) \\  & =3{y}^{2}-24y+48.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $P(y)=3{y}^{2}-24y+48.$

Question 6
?

The quadratic polynomial P(y) has the double root y1=y2=4, and the coefficient of the quadratic term is a=3. Find P(y).

a
3y2−4y+24
b
3y2−12y+32
c
3y2−8y+16
d
3y2−24y+48
e
3y2−3y+96
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

Since our quadratic polynomial has the double root y1=y2=4, and the coefficient of the quadratic term is a=3, we can write the polynomial as follows:

a(y−y1)2=3(y−4)2

Expanding the parentheses, we obtain

3(y−4)2=3(y2−8y+16)=3y2−24y+48.

Therefore, P(y)=3y2−24y+48.

verification.explanation: The revealed solution confirms P(y)=3(y-4)^2=3(y^2-8y+16)=3y^2-24y+48, matching option d.

content.knowledge_point: Finding a Quadratic Polynomial Given a Double Root and a Leading Coefficient
content.problem: The quadratic polynomial $P(y)$ has the double root ${y}_{1}={y}_{2}=4,$ and the coefficient of the quadratic term is $a=3.$ Find $P(y).$
content.worked_solution:
Since our quadratic polynomial has the double root ${y}_{1}={y}_{2}=4,$ and the coefficient of the quadratic term is $a=3,$ we can write the polynomial as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}a(y-{y}_{1})^{2} & =3{(y-4)}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the parentheses, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}3{(y-4)}^{2} & =3({y}^{2}-8y+16) \\  & =3{y}^{2}-24y+48.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $P(y)=3{y}^{2}-24y+48.$

after.name: Question 7
after.problem: The quadratic polynomial $P(x)$ has the double root ${x}_{1}={x}_{2}=-\frac{2}{3},$ and the coefficient of the quadratic term is $a=9.$ Find $P(x).$
after.worked_solution:
Since our quadratic polynomial has the double root ${x}_{1}={x}_{2}=-\frac{2}{3},$ and the coefficient of the quadratic term is $a=9,$ we can write the polynomial as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}a(x-{x}_{1})^{2} & =9{(x-(-\frac{2}{3}))}^{2} \\  & =9{(x+\frac{2}{3})}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the parentheses, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}9{(x+\frac{2}{3})}^{2} & =9({x}^{2}+\frac{4}{3}x+\frac{4}{9}) \\  & =9{x}^{2}+12x+4.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $P(x)=9{x}^{2}+12x+4.$

Question 7

The quadratic polynomial P(x) has the double root x1=x2=−23, and the coefficient of the quadratic term is a=9. Find P(x).

a
9x2−6x−4
b
9x2+12x+4
c
9x2−12x+4
d
9x2+6x−12
e
9x2−6x+6
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Since our quadratic polynomial has the double root x1=x2=−23, and the coefficient of the quadratic term is a=9, we can write the polynomial as follows:

a(x−x1)2=9(x−(−23))2=9(x+23)2

Expanding the parentheses, we obtain

9(x+23)2=9(x2+43x+49)=9x2+12x+4.

Therefore, P(x)=9x2+12x+4.

content.knowledge_point: Finding a Quadratic Polynomial Given a Double Root and a Leading Coefficient
content.problem: The quadratic polynomial $P(x)$ has the double root ${x}_{1}={x}_{2}=-\frac{2}{3},$ and the coefficient of the quadratic term is $a=9.$ Find $P(x).$
content.worked_solution:
Since our quadratic polynomial has the double root ${x}_{1}={x}_{2}=-\frac{2}{3},$ and the coefficient of the quadratic term is $a=9,$ we can write the polynomial as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}a(x-{x}_{1})^{2} & =9{(x-(-\frac{2}{3}))}^{2} \\  & =9{(x+\frac{2}{3})}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the parentheses, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}9{(x+\frac{2}{3})}^{2} & =9({x}^{2}+\frac{4}{3}x+\frac{4}{9}) \\  & =9{x}^{2}+12x+4.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $P(x)=9{x}^{2}+12x+4.$

after.name: Question 9
after.problem: The quadratic polynomial $P(y)$ has the double root ${y}_{1}={y}_{2}=-5,$ and the coefficient of the quadratic term is $a=-2.$ Find $P(y).$
after.worked_solution:
Since our quadratic polynomial has the double root ${y}_{1}={y}_{2}=-5,$ and the coefficient of the quadratic term is $a=-2,$ we can write the polynomial as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}a(y-{y}_{1})^{2} & =(-2){(y-(-5))}^{2} \\  & =(-2){(y+5)}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the parentheses, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}(-2){(y+5)}^{2} & =(-2)({y}^{2}+10y+25) \\  & =-2{y}^{2}-20y-50.\end{aligned}
$$

The quadratic polynomial P(y) has the double root y1=y2=−5, and the coefficient of the quadratic term is a=−2. Find P(y).

a
−2y2−10y+50
b
−2y2+20y−50
c
−2y2+20y+50
d
−2y2−20y−50
e
−2y2+10y−50
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Since our quadratic polynomial has the double root y1=y2=−5, and the coefficient of the quadratic term is a=−2, we can write the polynomial as follows:

a(y−y1)2=(−2)(y−(−5))2=(−2)(y+5)2

Expanding the parentheses, we obtain

(−2)(y+5)2=(−2)(y2+10y+25)=−2y2−20y−50.

Therefore, P(y)=−2y2−20y−50.

content.knowledge_point: Finding a Quadratic Polynomial Given a Double Root and a Leading Coefficient
content.problem: The quadratic polynomial $P(y)$ has the double root ${y}_{1}={y}_{2}=-5,$ and the coefficient of the quadratic term is $a=-2.$ Find $P(y).$
content.worked_solution:
Since our quadratic polynomial has the double root ${y}_{1}={y}_{2}=-5,$ and the coefficient of the quadratic term is $a=-2,$ we can write the polynomial as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}a(y-{y}_{1})^{2} & =(-2){(y-(-5))}^{2} \\  & =(-2){(y+5)}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the parentheses, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}(-2){(y+5)}^{2} & =(-2)({y}^{2}+10y+25) \\  & =-2{y}^{2}-20y-50.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $P(y)=-2{y}^{2}-20y-50.$

after.name: Question 11
after.problem: The quadratic polynomial $f(z)$ has real coefficients, has roots ${z}_{1}=2\text{i}$ and ${z}_{2}=-2\text{i},$ and the coefficient of the quadratic term is $1.$ Find $f(z).$
after.worked_solution:
Since our quadratic polynomial has roots ${z}_{1}=2\text{i}$ and ${z}_{2}=-2\text{i},$ and the coefficient of the quadratic term is $a=1,$ we can write the polynomial as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}a(z-{z}_{1})(z-{z}_{2}) & =(1)(z-2\text{i})(z-(-2\text{i})) \\  & =(z-2\text{i})(z+2\text{i})\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the parentheses, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}(z-2\text{i})(z+2\text{i}) & ={z}^{2}-(2\text{i})^{2} \\  & ={z}^{2}-4{\text{i}}^{2} \\  & ={z}^{2}+4.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $f(z)={z}^{2}+4.$

Question 11
?

The quadratic polynomial f(z) has real coefficients, has roots z1=2i and z2=−2i, and the coefficient of the quadratic term is 1. Find f(z).

a
z2+1
b
z2+2
c
z2+4
d
z2−2
e
z2−4
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Since our quadratic polynomial has roots z1=2i and z2=−2i, and the coefficient of the quadratic term is a=1, we can write the polynomial as follows:

a(z−z1)(z−z2)=(1)(z−2i)(z−(−2i))=(z−2i)(z+2i)

Expanding the parentheses, we obtain

(z−2i)(z+2i)=z2−(2i)2=z2−4i2=z2+4.

Therefore, f(z)=z2+4.

content.knowledge_point: Finding a Quadratic Polynomial Given Two Imaginary or Complex Roots
content.problem: The quadratic polynomial $f(z)$ has real coefficients, has roots ${z}_{1}=2\text{i}$ and ${z}_{2}=-2\text{i},$ and the coefficient of the quadratic term is $1.$ Find $f(z).$
content.worked_solution:
Since our quadratic polynomial has roots ${z}_{1}=2\text{i}$ and ${z}_{2}=-2\text{i},$ and the coefficient of the quadratic term is $a=1,$ we can write the polynomial as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}a(z-{z}_{1})(z-{z}_{2}) & =(1)(z-2\text{i})(z-(-2\text{i})) \\  & =(z-2\text{i})(z+2\text{i})\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the parentheses, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}(z-2\text{i})(z+2\text{i}) & ={z}^{2}-(2\text{i})^{2} \\  & ={z}^{2}-4{\text{i}}^{2} \\  & ={z}^{2}+4.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $f(z)={z}^{2}+4.$

Question 13
?

The quadratic polynomial f(z) has real coefficients, has roots z1=4i and z2=−4i, and the coefficient of the quadratic term is −1. Find f(z).

a
−z2+16
b
−z2+4
c
−z2−8
d
−z2−4
e
−z2−16
Submit

decision.explanation: With leading coefficient -1, f(z)=-(z-4i)(z+4i)=-(z^2+16)=-z^2-16, since i^2=-1. This matches option e.

after.name: Question 13
after.problem: The quadratic polynomial $f(z)$ has real coefficients, has roots ${z}_{1}=4\text{i}$ and ${z}_{2}=-4\text{i},$ and the coefficient of the quadratic term is $-1.$ Find $f(z).$
after.worked_solution:
Since our quadratic polynomial has roots ${z}_{1}=4\text{i}$ and ${z}_{2}=-4\text{i},$ and the coefficient of the quadratic term is $a=-1,$ we can write the polynomial as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}a(z-{z}_{1})(z-{z}_{2}) & =(-1)(z-4\text{i})(z-(-4\text{i})) \\  & =-(z-4\text{i})(z+4\text{i})\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the parentheses, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}-(z-4\text{i})(z+4\text{i}) & =-({z}^{2}-(4\text{i})^{2}) \\  & =-({z}^{2}-16{\text{i}}^{2}) \\  & =-({z}^{2}+16) \\  & =-{z}^{2}-16.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $f(z)=-{z}^{2}-16.$

Question 13

The quadratic polynomial f(z) has real coefficients, has roots z1=4i and z2=−4i, and the coefficient of the quadratic term is −1. Find f(z).

a
−z2+16
b
−z2+4
c
−z2−8
d
−z2−4
e
−z2−16
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Since our quadratic polynomial has roots z1=4i and z2=−4i, and the coefficient of the quadratic term is a=−1, we can write the polynomial as follows:

a(z−z1)(z−z2)=(−1)(z−4i)(z−(−4i))=−(z−4i)(z+4i)

Expanding the parentheses, we obtain

−(z−4i)(z+4i)=−(z2−(4i)2)=−(z2−16i2)=−(z2+16)=−z2−16.

Therefore, f(z)=−z2−16.

after.name: Question 14
after.problem: The quadratic polynomial $f(z)$ has real coefficients, has roots ${z}_{1}=3+2\text{i}$ and ${z}_{2}=3-2\text{i},$ and the coefficient of the quadratic term is $-2.$ Find $f(z).$
after.worked_solution:
Since our quadratic polynomial has roots ${z}_{1}=3+2\text{i}$ and ${z}_{2}=3-2\text{i},$ and the coefficient of the quadratic term is $a=-2,$ we can write the polynomial as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}a(z-{z}_{1})(z-{z}_{2}) & =(-2)(z-(3+2\text{i}))(z-(3-2\text{i}))\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the parentheses, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}(-2)(z-(3+2\text{i}))(z-(3-2\text{i})) & =(-2)({z}^{2}-(3+2\text{i})z-(3-2\text{i})z+(3+2\text{i})(3-2\text{i})) \\  & =(-2)({z}^{2}-(3+2\text{i}+3-2\text{i})z+({3}^{2}-{2}^{2}{\text{i}}^{2})) \\  & =(-2)({z}^{2}-6z+(9+4)) \\  & =-2{z}^{2}+12z-26.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $f(z)=-2{z}^{2}+12z-26.$

a(z−z1)(z−z2)=(−2)(z−(3+2i))(z−(3−2i))

decision.explanation: The conjugate roots give f(y)=2((y-4)^2+1)=2(y^2-8y+17)=2y^2-16y+34, matching option d.

after.name: Question 15
after.problem: The quadratic polynomial $f(y)$ has real coefficients, has roots ${y}_{1}=4+\text{i}$ and ${y}_{2}=4-\text{i},$ and the coefficient of the quadratic term is $2.$ Find $f(y).$
after.worked_solution:
Since our quadratic polynomial has roots ${y}_{1}=4+\text{i}$ and ${y}_{2}=4-\text{i},$ and the coefficient of the quadratic term is $a=2,$ we can write the polynomial as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}a(y-{y}_{1})(y-{y}_{2}) & =2(y-(4+\text{i}))(y-(4-\text{i}))\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the parentheses, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}2(y-(4+\text{i}))(y-(4-\text{i})) & =2({y}^{2}-(4+\text{i})y-(4-\text{i})y+(4+\text{i})(4-\text{i})) \\  & =2({y}^{2}-(4+\text{i}+4-\text{i})y+({4}^{2}-{\text{i}}^{2})) \\  & =2({y}^{2}-8y+(16+1)) \\  & =2{y}^{2}-16y+34.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $f(y)=2{y}^{2}-16y+34.$

Question 15

The quadratic polynomial f(y) has real coefficients, has roots y1=4+i and y2=4−i, and the coefficient of the quadratic term is 2. Find f(y).

a
2y2−12y+16
b
2y2+8y−17
c
2y2+16y−34
d
2y2−16y+34
e
2y2−8y+17
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Since our quadratic polynomial has roots y1=4+i and y2=4−i, and the coefficient of the quadratic term is a=2, we can write the polynomial as follows:

a(y−y1)(y−y2)=2(y−(4+i))(y−(4−i))

Expanding the parentheses, we obtain

2(y−(4+i))(y−(4−i))=2(y2−(4+i)y−(4−i)y+(4+i)(4−i))=2(y2−(4+i+4−i)y+(42−i2))=2(y2−8y+(16+1))=2y2−16y+34.

Therefore, f(y)=2y2−16y+34.

after.name: Question 16
after.problem: Which of the following is a factor of $-{v}^{2}+12v-45?$
after.worked_solution:
First, we let $f(v)=-{v}^{2}+12v-45.$

Next, we solve $f(v)=0$ by completing the square, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(v) & =0 \\ -{v}^{2}+12v-45 & =0 \\ {v}^{2}-12v+45 & =0 \\ ({v}^{2}-2\cdot 6\cdot v+{6}^{2})-{6}^{2}+45 & =0 \\ (v-6)^{2}-36+45 & =0 \\ (v-6)^{2}+9 & =0 \\ (v-6)^{2} & =-9 \\ (v-6)^{2} & =9{\text{i}}^{2} \\ (v-6)^{2} & =(3\text{i})^{2} \\ v-6 & =\pm 3\text{i} \\ v & =6\pm 3\text{i}\end{aligned}
$$

Since our quadratic equation has roots ${v}_{1}=6+3\text{i}$ and ${v}_{2}=6-3\text{i},$ and the coefficient of the quadratic term is $a=-1,$ the expression $-{v}^{2}+12v-45$ can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}-{v}^{2}+12v-45 & =a(v-{v}_{1})(v-{v}_{2}) \\  & =-(v-(6+3\text{i}))(v-(6-3\text{i})).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, among the given options, only $v-(6-3\text{i})$ is a factor of $-{v}^{2}+12v-45.$

Next, we solve f(v)=0 by completing the square, as follows:

f(v)=0−v2+12v−45=0v2−12v+45=0(v2−2⋅6⋅v+62)−62+45=0(v−6)2−36+45=0(v−6)2+9=0(v−6)2=−9(v−6)2=9i2(v−6)2=(3i)2v−6=±3iv=6±3i

Since our quadratic equation has roots v1=6+3i and v2=6−3i, and the coefficient of the quadratic term is a=−1, the expression −v2+12v−45 can be written as

−v2+12v−45=a(v−v1)(v−v2)=−(v−(6+3i))(v−(6−3i)).

Therefore, among the given options, only v−(6−3i) is a factor of −v2+12v−45.

after.name: Question 17
after.problem: Which of the following is a factor of ${u}^{2}-2u+5?$
after.worked_solution:
First, we let $f(u)={u}^{2}-2u+5.$

Next, we solve $f(u)=0$ by completing the square, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(u) & =0 \\ {u}^{2}-2u+5 & =0 \\ ({u}^{2}-2\cdot u+{1}^{2})-{1}^{2}+5 & =0 \\ (u-1)^{2}+4 & =0 \\ (u-1)^{2} & =-4 \\ (u-1)^{2} & =4{\text{i}}^{2} \\ (u-1)^{2} & =(2\text{i})^{2} \\ u-1 & =\pm 2\text{i} \\ u & =1\pm 2\text{i}\end{aligned}
$$

Since our quadratic equation has roots ${u}_{1}=1+2\text{i}$ and ${u}_{2}=1-2\text{i},$ and the coefficient of the quadratic term is $a=1,$ the expression ${u}^{2}-2u+5$ can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}{u}^{2}-2u+5 & =a(u-{u}_{1})(u-{u}_{2}) \\  & =(u-(1+2\text{i}))(u-(1-2\text{i})).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, among the given options, only $u-(1-2\text{i})$ is a factor of ${u}^{2}-2u+5.$

Next, we solve f(u)=0 by completing the square, as follows:

f(u)=0u2−2u+5=0(u2−2⋅u+12)−12+5=0(u−1)2+4=0(u−1)2=−4(u−1)2=4i2(u−1)2=(2i)2u−1=±2iu=1±2i

u2−2u+5=a(u−u1)(u−u2)=(u−(1+2i))(u−(1−2i)).

Therefore, among the given options, only u−(1−2i) is a factor of u2−2u+5.

decision.explanation: 3x^2-6x+51=3((x-1)^2+16), so its roots are 1±4i. The factorization is 3(x-(1+4i))(x-(1-4i)), matching option d.

after.name: Question 18
after.worked_solution:
First, we let $f(x)=3{x}^{2}-6x+51.$

Next, we solve $f(x)=0$ by completing the square, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =0 \\ 3{x}^{2}-6x+51 & =0 \\ {x}^{2}-2x+17 & =0 \\ ({x}^{2}-2\cdot 1\cdot x+{1}^{2})-{1}^{2}+17 & =0 \\ (x-1)^{2}-1+17 & =0 \\ (x-1)^{2}+16 & =0 \\ (x-1)^{2} & =-16 \\ (x-1)^{2} & =16{\text{i}}^{2} \\ (x-1)^{2} & =(4\text{i})^{2} \\ x-1 & =\pm 4\text{i} \\ x & =1\pm 4\text{i}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since our quadratic equation has roots ${x}_{1}=1+4\text{i}$ and ${x}_{2}=1-4\text{i},$ and the coefficient of the quadratic term is $a=3,$ the expression $3{x}^{2}-6x+51$ can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}3{x}^{2}-6x+51 & =a(x-{x}_{1})(x-{x}_{2}) \\  & =3(x-(1+4\text{i}))(x-(1-4\text{i})).\end{aligned}
$$

Factor 3x2−6x+51.

a
3(x−(1−4i))2
b
(x−(2+3i))2

3(x−(2+3i))(x−(2−3i))
d
3(x−(1+4i))(x−(1−4i))
e
(x−(2+4i))(x−(2−4i))
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we let f(x)=3x2−6x+51.

Next, we solve f(x)=0 by completing the square, as follows:

f(x)=03x2−6x+51=0x2−2x+17=0(x2−2⋅1⋅x+12)−12+17=0(x−1)2−1+17=0(x−1)2+16=0(x−1)2=−16(x−1)2=16i2(x−1)2=(4i)2x−1=±4ix=1±4i

Now, since our quadratic equation has roots x1=1+4i and x2=1−4i, and the coefficient of the quadratic term is a=3, the expression 3x2−6x+51 can be written as

3x2−6x+51=a(x−x1)(x−x2)=3(x−(1+4i))(x−(1−4i)).

First, we let $f(x)=3{x}^{2}-6x+51.$

Next, we solve $f(x)=0$ by completing the square, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =0 \\ 3{x}^{2}-6x+51 & =0 \\ {x}^{2}-2x+17 & =0 \\ ({x}^{2}-2\cdot 1\cdot x+{1}^{2})-{1}^{2}+17 & =0 \\ (x-1)^{2}-1+17 & =0 \\ (x-1)^{2}+16 & =0 \\ (x-1)^{2} & =-16 \\ (x-1)^{2} & =16{\text{i}}^{2} \\ (x-1)^{2} & =(4\text{i})^{2} \\ x-1 & =\pm 4\text{i} \\ x & =1\pm 4\text{i}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since our quadratic equation has roots ${x}_{1}=1+4\text{i}$ and ${x}_{2}=1-4\text{i},$ and the coefficient of the quadratic term is $a=3,$ the expression $3{x}^{2}-6x+51$ can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}3{x}^{2}-6x+51 & =a(x-{x}_{1})(x-{x}_{2}) \\  & =3(x-(1+4\text{i}))(x-(1-4\text{i})).\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 19
after.problem: Which of the following is a factor of $3{z}^{2}-24z+75?$
after.worked_solution:
First, we let $f(z)=3{z}^{2}-24z+75.$

Next, we solve $f(z)=0$ by completing the square, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(z) & =0 \\ 3{z}^{2}-24z+75 & =0 \\ {z}^{2}-8z+25 & =0 \\ ({z}^{2}-2\cdot 4\cdot z+{4}^{2})-{4}^{2}+25 & =0 \\ (z-4)^{2}-16+25 & =0 \\ (z-4)^{2}+9 & =0 \\ (z-4)^{2} & =-9 \\ (z-4)^{2} & =9{\text{i}}^{2} \\ (z-4)^{2} & =(3\text{i})^{2} \\ z-4 & =\pm 3\text{i} \\ z & =4\pm 3\text{i}\end{aligned}
$$

Since our quadratic equation has roots ${z}_{1}=4+3\text{i}$ and ${z}_{2}=4-3\text{i},$ and the coefficient of the quadratic term is $a=3,$ the expression $3{z}^{2}-24z+75$ can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}3{z}^{2}-24z+75 & =a(z-{z}_{1})(z-{z}_{2}) \\  & =3(z-(4+3\text{i}))(z-(4-3\text{i})).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, among the given options, only $z-(4-3\text{i})$ is a factor of $3{z}^{2}-24z+75.$

Which of the following is a factor of 3z2−24z+75?

a
z−(3−4i)
b
z−(4−3i)
c
z−(2−i)
d
z−(1−2i)
e
z−(7−2i)
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

First, we let f(z)=3z2−24z+75.

Next, we solve f(z)=0 by completing the square, as follows:

f(z)=03z2−24z+75=0z2−8z+25=0(z2−2⋅4⋅z+42)−42+25=0(z−4)2−16+25=0(z−4)2+9=0(z−4)2=−9(z−4)2=9i2(z−4)2=(3i)2z−4=±3iz=4±3i

Since our quadratic equation has roots z1=4+3i and z2=4−3i, and the coefficient of the quadratic term is a=3, the expression 3z2−24z+75 can be written as

3z2−24z+75=a(z−z1)(z−z2)=3(z−(4+3i))(z−(4−3i)).

Therefore, among the given options, only z−(4−3i) is a factor of 3z2−24z+75.

content.knowledge_point: Factoring a Quadratic Polynomial With Complex Roots
content.problem: Which of the following is a factor of $3{z}^{2}-24z+75?$
content.worked_solution:
First, we let $f(z)=3{z}^{2}-24z+75.$

Next, we solve $f(z)=0$ by completing the square, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(z) & =0 \\ 3{z}^{2}-24z+75 & =0 \\ {z}^{2}-8z+25 & =0 \\ ({z}^{2}-2\cdot 4\cdot z+{4}^{2})-{4}^{2}+25 & =0 \\ (z-4)^{2}-16+25 & =0 \\ (z-4)^{2}+9 & =0 \\ (z-4)^{2} & =-9 \\ (z-4)^{2} & =9{\text{i}}^{2} \\ (z-4)^{2} & =(3\text{i})^{2} \\ z-4 & =\pm 3\text{i} \\ z & =4\pm 3\text{i}\end{aligned}
$$

Since our quadratic equation has roots ${z}_{1}=4+3\text{i}$ and ${z}_{2}=4-3\text{i},$ and the coefficient of the quadratic term is $a=3,$ the expression $3{z}^{2}-24z+75$ can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}3{z}^{2}-24z+75 & =a(z-{z}_{1})(z-{z}_{2}) \\  & =3(z-(4+3\text{i}))(z-(4-3\text{i})).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, among the given options, only $z-(4-3\text{i})$ is a factor of $3{z}^{2}-24z+75.$
